proceedings.supporting_quote: on 5 October 1995 property belonging to the applicant - the ship Stavanger and a floating drydock - was frozen on the order of the Nizhniy Novgorod prosecutor’s office.
In January 1996 the Port transferred the sum of 2.5 million US dollars to a special account of the Nizhniy Novgorod city administration.
on 11 March 1996 the proceeds from the ship sale were frozen on the order of the Nizhniy Novgorod prosecutor’s office.
On 18 May 1996 the Nizhniy Novgorod prosecutor’s office unfroze the account and transferred the money to the yard.
By a judgment of the Nizhniy Novgorod Regional Court of 21 April 1997... the applicant was ordered to pay the “Oka” damages
On 21 April 1997 the Nizhniy Novgorod Regional Court found the applicant guilty on some of the charges
In July 1997 the Supreme Court quashed the conviction on the applicant’s appeal and remitted the case to the Nizhniy Novgorod Regional Court
On 1 April 1998 the local electoral committee declared the elections invalid
On 19 May the applicant’s “civil defender” requested the Regional Court to dismiss the judge presiding in the case for bias... Both requests were rejected by the Regional Court.
On the same day the applicant requested to admit Mrs Moskalenko as his lawyer in the trial... Both requests were rejected by the Regional Court.
On 23 April 1998 the applicant’s “civil defender”... lodged with the Supreme Court an appeal against the court order of 2 April to detain the applicant.
During the second trial, on 27 May 1998... the applicant was ordered by the Nizhniy Novgorod Court to pay damages to “Oka”
On 27 May 1998 the Regional Court made a number of further orders ( частные определения ) in the case.
On 27 May 1998 the Nizhniy Novgorod Regional Court issued an order ( частное определение ) in which it noted that the investigators had violated the Code of Criminal Procedure (CCP)
On 27 May 1998 the Nizhniy Novgorod Regional Court found the applicant guilty on charges of misappropriation and embezzlement, larceny, bribery and attempt not to return money from abroad.
It appears that on 8 July 1998 the Regional Court ordered that the applicant should be given the amended version
On 10 August 1998 the Supreme Court confirmed the judgment of the Nizhniy Novgorod Regional Court, with some alterations.
In February 1999 the applicant’s first (1982) conviction was quashed, and the file in that case was closed by the Nizhniy Novgorod regional prosecutor’s office.
An appeal to the Supreme Court by the applicant’s lawyer, Mr. O., challenged the judgment on a number of points.
